questions.prompt: Complete this line from the portrait: "She now ___ in Sousse with her husband and their two sons."

options.text: lives
lived
has lived
was living

questions.explanation: "now" marks a fact that is still true today, and a fact that is still true takes the present simple: "lives". "lived" and "was living" close the fact in the past, and "has lived" would need a starting point such as "since 2018" to count a period that continues.

questions.prompt: Your classmate has just listened to Nour's latest record, and you want her opinion of it. Which question do you ask?

options.text: Would you like it?
Do you know it well?
Would you like to buy it one day?
What do you think of it?

questions.explanation: Asking for an opinion uses "What do you think of it?", with "of" because you want a judgement. "Would you like it?" and "Would you like to buy it one day?" ask about a wish, not about an opinion, and "Do you know it well?" only asks whether she knows the record.

questions.prompt: Nour is paid a lot for her concerts, and last month she came first in a big competition. Which sentence reports both facts correctly?

options.text: She wins a lot of money and wins a big prize.
She earns a lot of money and wins a big prize.
She wins a lot of money and earns a big prize.
She earns a lot of money and earns a big prize.

questions.explanation: You earn money by working, and you win a prize, a match or a game, so the correct sentence is "She earns a lot of money and wins a big prize." Every version with "wins a lot of money" uses the verb of competitions for a salary, and "earns a big prize" uses the verb of salaries for a competition.

questions.prompt: Nour has a rule: no television, ever — from her first song until today. Which sentence reports that as a total?

options.text: Nour never gave a television interview in 2015.
Nour was never giving a television interview.
Nour has never given a television interview.
Nour never gives a television interview.

questions.explanation: A total that runs from the start of a career until today takes the present perfect, so the answer is "Nour has never given a television interview." "Nour never gives a television interview." reports a present habit, "Nour was never giving a television interview." puts the fact in the past, and "Nour never gave a television interview in 2015." limits the total to one single year.

questions.prompt: A friend says: "Publicity is bad for a singer." You think the opposite and you want to answer politely. Which reply do you choose?

options.text: I'm afraid I can't agree.
I agree with you completely.
That's true, you're right.
I am not agree with you at all.

questions.explanation: A polite refusal of somebody's opinion is "I'm afraid I can't agree.", which softens the disagreement. "I agree with you completely." and "That's true, you're right." agree instead of disagreeing, and "I am not agree with you at all." treats "agree" as an adjective: the correct negative form is "I don't agree".

questions.prompt: Read this portrait: "Everybody calls her Nour, but her real name is Nour Belhaj Amara. She was born in Bizerte in 1994, and she now lives in Sousse with her husband and their two sons. She is a singer and a songwriter. She sang her first songs with her grandmother, and she recorded her first album in a friend's garage in 2015. Since then she has released three more records and has toured in six countries. She has never given a television interview." Which title fits the whole text best?

options.text: She Recorded Her First Album in a Garage
The World of Music
A Rising Career, Far from the Cameras
Two Sons and a Husband

questions.explanation: A good title carries the main idea of the whole text, and this text puts her growing career next to her refusal of television, so "A Rising Career, Far from the Cameras" covers both. "She Recorded Her First Album in a Garage" is a full sentence carrying one single fact, "Two Sons and a Husband" keeps one detail of her family, and "The World of Music" is so vague that it would fit any text about a singer.
